question: Your customer support resolution agent now uses a coordinator agent with three subagents: one for account lookups, one for order lookups, and one for refunds. Currently the refund subagent asks the order subagent for order details directly. It also calls escalate_to_human on its own whenever process_refund returns an error. Support leads cannot see why some refund cases were escalated, and similar failures are handled differently across cases. Which design change best addresses these problems?

options.text: Route every subagent request, result, and error through the coordinator agent, which applies one error-handling policy and decides what information each subagent receives.
options.reason: In a hub-and-spoke architecture the coordinator manages all inter-subagent communication, error handling, and information routing, which gives observability and consistent error handling.

options.text: Give the refund subagent the coordinator agent's full conversation history so that it can make its own escalation decisions with complete customer context.
options.reason: Subagents do not inherit the coordinator's history automatically, and this change keeps escalation decisions inside the subagent, outside the coordinator's view and error handling.

options.text: Have each subagent record every direct call it makes to another subagent in a shared log file, while each subagent keeps its own rules for handling tool errors and escalations.
options.reason: Subagents still talk to each other directly and handle errors separately, so communication and error handling are not managed by the coordinator as the hub-and-spoke pattern requires.

options.text: Have the refund subagent retry process_refund several times with exponential backoff and call escalate_to_human only after every retry has failed.
options.reason: Error handling and escalation stay inside the subagent, so the coordinator still cannot observe failures or handle them consistently across cases.
